card.name: Commas after eye-contact conditions
card.fires_on: The comma (or nearby word) right after an eye-exposure clause, such as "if eye contact occurs," or "gets in eyes,", in warnings about irritant drugs. It also fires on "eye" itself and on "causes" in eye-injury sentences.

modes.label: Comma after eye exposure
modes.description: Comma ending an "if ... eyes" clause, just before rinsing instructions.
